title: A parts import row with a number already stocked here updates that part
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete', See Financial Data and the Data Import setting.
  • Part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-IMPDUP-01), with the description {Description-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL Import Dup), is stocked at {Location-A} with Min 1 and Max 5, and 3 in its bin {Bin-A} (for example General Storage).
  • {Number-A} (for example zzautotest.pl.impdup.01) matches {Part-A} once upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces are ignored.
  • No other Part Library entry has a number that matches {Part-A} in that way.
  • {Word-A} (for example IMPDUP) is a part of the number that both {Part-A} and {Number-A} contain.
  • Import file {File-A} (for example ZZ-PL-IMPDUP-1.csv) holds one row: part number {Part-A}, description {Description-A}, Min 2, Max 6, quantity 3 and Bin Location {Bin-A}.
  • Import file {File-B} (for example ZZ-PL-IMPDUP-2.csv) holds the same row with part number {Number-A}, Min 3 and Max 7.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings → Data Import → Inventory.
  2. Upload {File-A}.
  3. Run the import.
  4. Go to Parts → Inventory and type {Word-A} in the search.
  5. Go to Settings → Data Import → Inventory.
  6. Upload {File-B}.
  7. Run the import.
  8. Go to Parts → Inventory and type {Word-A} in the search.
  9. Click the Inactive tab.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: the import finishes and does not refuse the row: no "already exists at this location" message appears.
  • Step 4: one row, {Part-A}, now with Min 2 and Max 6 (it had 1 and 5): the row updated the part already stocked here.
  • Step 7: the import finishes and does not refuse the row, although {Number-A} differs from {Part-A} in upper and lower case and punctuation.
  • Step 8: still one row, numbered {Part-A} exactly as before, now with Min 3 and Max 7. No second part was added.
  • Step 9: no row for it on the Inactive tab either.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S7-N7, S13-N9a, §2 Out of scope (parts CSV import matching), read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas: no board shows the parts import (13 Oct copy). Product's answer of 13 Oct (Chris Ward, question 3). Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S7-N7: “S7-N3 to S7-N6 do not apply to the parts CSV import. An import row whose number matches a part already stocked at this location updates that part (S13-N9a). It is never refused for a duplicate number.”
  • S13-N9a: “When an import row's number matches a Part Library entry that is already stocked as a part at this location, the import updates that part. It never adds a second part on the same entry. A match ignores upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces, so re-importing an old number that differs from the new one only in those ways updates the renamed part.”
  • PRD §2 Out of scope (parts CSV import matching): “The import matches a number ignoring upper and lower case. If nothing matches, it also ignores hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces. It writes the row's description onto the entry it matches. It never moves a part to a different entry and never changes an entry's part number (S13-N9).”
